TEXT.English: [TAB]The Code of Hammurabi (Codex Hammurabi ) is a well-preserved ancient law code, created ca. 1760 BC (middle chronology) in ancient Babylon. It was enacted by the sixth Babylonian king, Hammurabi.[1] Only one example of the Code survives today, inscribed on a seven foot, four inch tall basalt stone slab or stele. Originally, several stelae would have been displayed in temples around the empire.

[COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]Hammurabi's Code[COLOR_REVERT] is the Babylonian replacement for the [COLOR_BUILDING_TEXT]Senate[COLOR_REVERT].
